title: The trick to lowering gas prices is driving less, US energy secretary says
summary:
Americans have been paying some of the highest prices for gas in years since the US attacked Iran in February.
US Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright, however, said, while making the rounds on the Sunday morning news shows, that despite the ongoing conflict, gas prices will soon go down because summer is ending.
"If I had to guess, they're more likely to go down than go up," Wright said of gas prices.
Gas prices first spiked after the US launched a surprise attack on Iran in February, and Iran responded by effectively shutting down the Strait of Hormuz.
The American Automobile Association said Labor Day weekend travelers are seeing the highest gas prices ever for this time of year.

title: Richard Hammond to find a way to share Welsh mansion with bats
summary:
Former Top Gear star Richard Hammond has said he will "find a way" of sharing his new £2m home with rare bats that have paused his renovation plans.
The 56-year-old bought the 19th Century Georgian mansion in Llanwenarth, near Abergavenny, in November 2025.
"If I have to share it with the bats, I'll find a way of sharing it with the bats," Hammond told BBC Wales.
"You don't move somewhere as beautiful as this and expect to stamp out everything that already lives there...
The survey ahead of the planned renovation work at the property identified a legal requirement to apply for a protected species development licence in order for it to continue.

title: Malaysia declares emergency in Sarawak as haze from Indonesia worsens
summary:
Share Malaysia declares emergency in Sarawak as haze from Indonesia worsens on social mediaMalaysia has declared a state of emergency in a district in Sarawak state after haze caused by wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia increased air pollution to “hazardous” levels.
The declaration followed a formal request from the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee after the region’s Air Pollutant Index reached levels warranting consideration of a local emergency.
The state’s disaster management authorities said a three-day cloud-seeding operation launched on Thursday would be extended to at least Monday, citing forecasts of “more conducive cloud formations” during that period.
Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee chairman Douglas Uggah Embas, speaking at a news conference in Kuching, stressed that the emergency applied only to Serian, not the entire state, but urged residents there to take the situation seriously.
Sarawak, in the northern part of Borneo island, has been heavily affected by haze for weeks, as have the neighbouring states of Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.

title: The Green Energy Paradox: Saving Nature by Destroying It
summary:
AdvertisementAs the Trump administration reverses elements of the previous administration's wind and solar policies, perhaps Americans should ask a question that has been strangely absent from the energy debate: Just how “green” is green energy?
Mining requires enormous quantities of heavy machinery, much of it diesel-powered.
What I object to is the marketing trick whereby one enormous industrial system is described as “dirty,” while another enormous industrial system is painted green and presented as if it descended from heaven on a leaf.
The technology advertised as saving nature requires mines, diesel machinery, steel, concrete, factories, transmission systems, and huge areas of land.
If saving nature requires destroying nature on an industrial scale, perhaps the first thing that needs recycling is our definition of environmentalism.
